headline: Blue Ridge Parkway Access and Biltmore Entry
reservation: Reservations are not required for Blue Ridge Parkway road access, but are essential for Biltmore Estate entry and specific Parkway campgrounds. During peak October foliage, accommodation near Asheville should be booked months in advance. Check the official NPS road map for seasonal closures or storm-related detours.

days.title: High Peaks and Mountain Craft

stops.name: Craggy Gardens
stops.detail: Visit the visitor center and walk the Craggy Pinnacle trail for 360-degree views of the Blue Ridge chain.

stops.name: Folk Art Center
stops.detail: Explore traditional Appalachian crafts and contemporary mountain art at this Parkway landmark.

days.driving: Allow 2.5 hours for the winding mountain miles; conditions vary with fog
days.note: Temperatures at Craggy Gardens can be 10-15 degrees cooler than in Asheville.

days.title: Estate History and Arboretum Walks

stops.name: Biltmore Estate
stops.detail: Tour the historic mansion and expansive formal gardens designed by Frederick Law Olmsted.

stops.name: North Carolina Arboretum
stops.detail: Walk through cultivated bonsai collections and forested trails adjacent to the Parkway.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour for local transfers; conditions vary
days.note: Biltmore requires timed entry tickets; allow ample time for the long driveway and shuttle.

days.title: Riverside Arts and Ridgeline Views

stops.name: River Arts District
stops.detail: Visit working artist studios in converted industrial buildings along the French Broad River.

stops.name: Mount Pisgah Overlook
stops.detail: Drive southwest on the Parkway to see the distinctive silhouette of one of the region's highest peaks.

days.driving: Allow 2 hours for the Parkway segment and town loops; conditions vary
days.note: Parkway sections southwest of Asheville may close during winter weather; verify status via NPS.

intel.title: Downtown vs Parkway
intel.text: Use parking garages in downtown Asheville for extended stays. Parkway overlooks have small lots that fill quickly during autumn weekends.

intel.title: High Elevation Gaps
intel.text: Cell service is frequently lost in the mountain gaps and tunnels of the Parkway. Don't rely on streaming navigation for remote trailheads.

intel.title: Parkway Fuel Absence
intel.text: There are no gas stations directly on the Blue Ridge Parkway. Ensure your tank is full before exiting Asheville or Black Mountain.

intel.title: Fog and Visibility
intel.text: Morning fog can significantly slow travel on the Parkway. If visibility is low, consider delaying your mountain drive until the afternoon.

intel.title: Tunnel Clearances
intel.text: The Parkway features numerous historic tunnels with limited height. Check official NPS height charts if driving an RV or high-clearance vehicle.

plan.arrival: Pick up your rental at Asheville Regional Airport (AVL), then drive 20-30 minutes north to central Asheville for supplies and check-in.
plan.vehicle: Standard cars are ideal for the Parkway's curves; RVs should check specific tunnel clearances and campground length limits.
plan.goldenHour: Craggy Gardens offers expansive western views for sunset, provided the mountain fog has cleared.
